column1: # phase 4-style settings encyclopedia: purview (added post-phase-7 coverage audit).
# Breadcrumb paths; portal deep-link verification tracked in docs/17 B6.

column8: desc
On by default for new tenants; if searches return nothing check the state first. Turning it on starts logging from that moment only: history before enablement does not exist.

column7: Purview portal > Audit > Policies > Audit retention policies
column8: Custom policies keep chosen record types or users longer than the default; one year needs Premium licensing and ten years its own add-on per user.

column4: Audit vs sign-in logs vs message trace
column8: Pick the tool by question: who touched content or settings = Audit; who authenticated from where = Entra sign-in logs; where is the email = message trace. Asking the wrong tool wastes an hour.

column7: Purview portal > Information protection > Label publishing policy settings
column8: Requires users to label documents and mail. Roll out only after label meanings are trained; mandatory-with-confused-users produces garbage labels that stick.

column4: Auto-labeling: client side vs service side
column8: Client side labels while users work in Office apps; service side labels data at rest in SharePoint OneDrive and Exchange. Service policies start in simulation: read the results before turning on.

column7: Purview portal > Information protection > Labels > Encryption
column8: Labels can encrypt with assigned rights. The tenant setting enabling co-authoring for encrypted files is one-way: it cannot be turned off once on. Plan before flipping.

column7: Purview portal > Data classification > Sensitive info types > Create
column8: Regex plus keywords plus confidence levels. Test against sample text from the SIT flyout before putting one in a DLP policy; a greedy pattern floods alerts tenant-wide.

column7: Purview portal > Data classification > EDM classifiers
column8: Match against your actual data table (hashed and uploaded) instead of patterns: near-zero false positives at the cost of a schema and refresh pipeline.

column7: Purview portal > Data classification > Trainable classifiers
column8: Pre-trained categories (resumes and source code and more) work immediately; custom ones need seed content and test feedback cycles before they are usable in policy.

column4: DLP policy modes: test then tips then on
column7: Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policy > Mode
column8: The rollout ladder: test silently first and read matches; add policy tips next so users see and can report false positives; enforce only after tuning. Skipping the ladder breaks business mail flows.

column7: Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Endpoint DLP settings
column8: Restricted apps and app groups; browser and service-domain restrictions; advanced classification. Devices must be onboarded (the same onboarding as Defender for Endpoint).

column4: DLP alerts live in the Defender portal
column8: DLP investigation moved to security.microsoft.com: alerts correlate into incidents there and the compliance portal only manages the policies. Tell the desk once and save everyone the hunt.

When policies and labels conflict: retention wins over deletion; then the longest retention period wins; then explicit inclusion beats implicit; finally the shortest deletion period wins. Answers most "why is this still here" tickets.

column7: Purview portal > Roles and scopes > Adaptive scopes
column8: Adaptive scopes are query-based membership (attributes) that track joiners and leavers on their own; static scopes are fixed location lists you maintain forever.

column7: Purview portal > Data lifecycle management > Import
column8: Network upload (free) or drive shipping into target mailboxes; pair the import with retention decisions so imported mail does not instantly violate policy.

column4: Hold vs retention: which stops deletion
column8: A hold preserves everything for a case including recoverable items and beats every retention or deletion policy while active. Retention governs normal lifecycle. Release order matters: check holds before blaming retention.
Content search and eDiscovery use KQL-style conditions: kind and participants and date ranges; exports have size and item limits per run. Test the query on one custodian before searching the tenant.

column4: IRM policy templates and the HR connector
column7: Purview portal > Insider risk management > Policies
column8: Templates like departing-employee data theft need their signals wired: the HR connector for resignation dates and DLP for exfil events. Adaptive protection can feed risk tiers into Conditional Access.

column4: Purview role groups vs Entra roles
column8: Purview permissions are role groups granted in the Purview portal (or Security & Compliance PowerShell) and invisible in Entra role assignments. eDiscovery Manager sees own cases; eDiscovery Administrator sees all. Audit Reader searches audit without broader compliance rights.

column4: Make Copilot safe: the readiness bundle
column8: Before Copilot: label the crown jewels; run the DSPM for AI oversharing assessment; fix broad SharePoint sharing (SharePoint Advanced Management helps); then monitor Copilot interactions in audit. Grounding permissions is the whole game: Copilot reads whatever the user already can.
